result.text: Study met primary endpoint: Day 30 all-cause mortality 23.7% (rezafungin) vs 21.3% (caspofungin), treatment difference 2.4% (95% CI -9.7%, 14.4%), within the 20% NI margin.

citations.quote: The study met its primary endpoint, with a Day 30 ACM rate of 23.7% in the rezafungin arm and 21.3% in the caspofungin arm in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) population, a treatment difference of 2.4% (95% CI -9.7%, 14.4%).

indication.text: Treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis in patients 18 years of age or older who have limited or no alternative options; approval based on limited clinical safety and efficacy data.

citations.quote: REZZAYO is indicated in patients 18 years of age or older who have limited or no alternative options for the treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis [see *Microbiology (12.4)*]. Approval of this indication is based on limited clinical safety and efficacy data for REZZAYO [see *Clinical Studies (14)*].

target_moa.text: Rezafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin that inhibits the 1,3-β-D-glucan synthase enzyme complex, blocking synthesis of 1,3-β-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall not present in mammalian cells.

citations.quote: Rezafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin. Rezafungin inhibits the 1,3-\beta-D-glucan synthase enzyme complex, which is present in fungal cell walls but not in mammalian cells.
REZZAYO is an echinocandin, a class of antifungal drugs that inhibits the synthesis of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of fungal cell walls.

Rezafungin acetate is a semisynthetic lipopeptide synthesized from a fermentation product of *Aspergillus nidulans*. REZZAYO is an echinocandin, a class of antifungal drugs that inhibits the synthesis of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of fungal cell walls.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) included hypokalemia (15%), pyrexia (12%), diarrhea (11%), anemia (10%), vomiting (9%) and nausea (9%). A neurotoxicity signal (tremors) was noted: tremors occurred in 4/151 (2.6%) rezafungin-treated patients vs none with caspofungin.

vote.text: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee convened January 24, 2023; voted 14 “yes”, 1 “no”, 0 abstentions on whether the benefit-risk assessment is favorable for treatment of candidemia/IC in adults with limited or no alternative treatment options.

citations.quote: A meeting of the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee was convened on January 24, 2023 to discuss this NDA. The committee was asked to vote on whether the overall benefit-risk assessment is favorable for the use of rezafungin for treatment of candidemia/IC in adults with limited or no alternative treatment options. There were 14 “yes” votes, 1 “no” vote, and 0 abstentions.

summary.text: Rezafungin was developed for candidemia/invasive candidiasis with orphan drug designation (2016) and QIDP plus Fast Track designations (June 27, 2017), and the NDA was reviewed under priority review as a new molecular entity with QIDP designation. It was a full (traditional) approval based on a single phase 3 noninferiority study (ReSTORE), and was discussed at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee.
